title: Short Stuff: Niagara Falls Dewatered
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1969 dewatering of the American Falls at Niagara Falls. Josh and Chuck cover the setting (American Falls, Bridal Veil Falls, Horseshoe Falls), the rock falls of the 1930s and 1950s that left boulders at the base, and the Army Corps of Engineers plan to dry the American Falls with a cofferdam diverting the Niagara River. Topics include the work done while dry (sandblasting, blue dye test, extensometers, monuments), the summer tourism, bodies and wish coins found in the riverbed, the reintroduction of water in November 1969, and a survey of residents that led to leaving the falls to nature. A listener correction about the summer of love date comes up along the way.
topics: Stuff You Should Know short stuff

segments.title: Opening banter and Niagara Falls overview
segments.summary: Hosts chat about visiting Niagara Falls and describe the three falls: American Falls, Bridal Veil Falls, and the larger Horseshoe Falls on the Canadian side. They note the current arrangement is only about 500 to 800 years old because of erosion.

segments.title: Rock falls and the decision to dry the American Falls
segments.summary: Rock falls in the 1930s and 1950s left boulders at the base of the American Falls. The Army Corps of Engineers decided the only way to assess the problem was to dry the falls. A cofferdam built near the fork diverted the Niagara River mostly toward Horseshoe Falls, with about 28,000 tons of fill.

segments.title: Work done on the dry riverbed
segments.summary: Crews kept the rock face wet with a sprinkler system from about June to November to prevent damage from drying. They sandblasted the rock, cleared loose gravel, and used blue dye to trace water flow. Extensometers measured movement of the rock, and metal monuments were installed for future surveys.

segments.title: Summer tourism, bodies, and wish coins
segments.summary: Visitors came to see the dry falls, with few in the first weekend and a weak tourist season overall. People walked on the riverbed and were chased off by the Army Corps. Crews found two bodies, including an unidentified woman in a red striped dress with a gold ring, and one deer carcass. People also collected wish coins from the riverbed.

segments.title: Summer of Love date correction
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a listener email correcting the year of the Summer of Love, which is 1967 rather than 1968 or 1969 as they had been saying.

segments.title: Refilling the falls and leaving them to nature
segments.summary: Water was turned back on slowly over a day in November 1969, which the hosts note was fifty years before the episode. A joint Canada-US commission surveyed about 2,000 residents, and most said to leave the falls to nature. Plans to turn off the water again in 2019 for bridge repairs were mentioned.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the idea of a live podcast from the brink and sign off the Short Stuff episode.
